ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the image there is a bordered card, and on the card there are only four statements. They are, in order: 1) Exactly one statement on this card is false; 2) Exactly two statements on this card are false; 3) Exactly three statements on this card are false; 4) Exactly four statements on this card are false. Then reason: Let the actual number of false statements be n. The four statements respectively claim n=1, n=2, n=3, n=4, so at most only one statement can be true, because n cannot simultaneously equal two different numbers. Also, if all four statements are false, then the 4th statement, "exactly four statements are false," would instead be true, a contradiction, so it is impossible for all four statements to be false. Therefore at least one statement is true. Combining this with "at most one statement is true," it can be known that exactly one statement is true, so there are 3 statements that are false. At this time the 3rd statement, "exactly three statements are false," is true, and the other three statements are false, completely consistent.

method.method_draft: Read from the image: the card contains four statements, respectively saying that exactly 1, 2, 3, or 4 statements on the card are false. Read from the text: we must determine how many of the four statements are actually false. Bridge: let n be the true number of false statements. Any statement that is true must match that same n, so two different statements cannot both be true. Also, if all four were false, then the fourth statement ('exactly four statements are false') would be true, so at least one statement is true. Therefore exactly one statement is true, which means 3 statements are false. The only consistent statement is the third one, so the answer is 3.
